definitions.explanation: An outstanding or highly acclaimed work of art, literature, film, or other creative endeavor.

examples.japanese: この{映画|えいが}は{名作|めいさく}だ。
{世界|せかい}の{名作|めいさく}を{集|あつ}めた{図書館|としょかん}がある。
examples.english: There's a library that has collected masterpieces from around the world.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}のころに{読|よ}んだ{名作|めいさく}を{大人|おとな}になって{読|よ}み{返|かえ}した。
examples.english: As an adult, I reread the classic works I had read as a child.

notes:
Applies broadly to literature, film, music, art, games, and other creative works. Often used in book/film series titles like {世界|せかい}{名作|めいさく}{劇場|げきじょう} (World Masterpiece Theater) or {名作|めいさく}{選|せん} (selection of classics).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {不朽|ふきゅう}の{名作|めいさく} — timeless masterpiece
- {隠|かく}れた{名作|めいさく} — hidden gem
- {名作|めいさく}{選|せん} — selection of classic works
- {名作|めいさく}と{呼|よ}ばれる — to be called a masterpiece

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {傑作|けっさく} — masterpiece (also means 'great joke/story')
- {大作|たいさく} — major work (emphasis on scale, not necessarily quality)
